prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1322; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained photographs of both vehicles. The rear damage is mostly consistent with the impact described, though a few old scratches on the bumper may predate this crash and are being noted separately.

Entry 4: Statements from two witnesses and the other driver all match the account of how the collision occurred. Nothing so far suggests the damage happened before coverage began.

Entry 5: Claimant joined the claim several days after the incident. No one at the scene recorded the claimant's name, so the claimant's presence in the vehicle is being confirmed through the other driver and witness accounts.

Entry 6: Claimant's description of events has been the same in every conversation so far. The reported shoulder injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Claimant disclosed a small strain to the same area several years ago, which healed fully according to prior records. Noted for the file and will be considered in evaluating the current injury.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records show steady progress with fewer visits over the last several weeks.

Entry 9: File summary: liability is clear, the reported injury is consistent with the mechanism of impact, and treatment has tapered as expected. Recommending continued handling of the injury component on the standard timeline.
